content: Feigning Protected Status: Some reports (contested) of Palestinian fighters wearing civilian clothes or using ambulances violated prohibitions on perfidy, though evidence was limited.

Testified to Human Rights Watch: 'The bulldozers came to our street on April 10. They started demolishing houses one by one. We could hear our neighbors screaming inside their homes as the bulldozers destroyed them. The soldiers wouldn't let us go help them. We heard the screams and then silence. I saw bodies pulled from the rubble days later.'

His son Muhammad shot dead on April 3 while walking with group of women and children toward hospital. Fayez testified: 'My son was with women and children. They were going to the hospital area. Israeli soldiers shot him twice in the face. He was 14 years old. There were no fighters with them. Just civilians trying to find safety.'
source: Human Rights Watch investigation; direct testimony

content: Testified about his father's death on April 10: 'My father was 57 years old and in a wheelchair. He was trying to get home. He was carrying a white flag. Israeli tanks shot him and then ran over him with the tank. We found his body crushed. There were no fighters near him. He was just an old disabled man trying to get home.'
source: Human Rights Watch documentation; Middle East Monitor

content: Testified to blocking of medical access: 'For 11 days we couldn't reach the wounded. Ambulances were fired upon. We had injured people inside the camp who needed urgent medical care. The Israelis wouldn't let us in. Some people died because they couldn't get medical treatment. This is a war crime—to prevent doctors from treating the wounded.'

After 9-day investigation with over 100 witness interviews: 'Israeli forces committed serious violations of international humanitarian law, some amounting prima facie to war crimes... The IDF used armored bulldozers to demolish buildings, in some cases with civilians inside... We documented direct attacks on medical personnel and prolonged denial of medical access.'
source: Human Rights Watch - Jenin: IDF Military Operations (May 2, 2002)

content: Defended operation: 'This was a nest of terrorism. It was an operation that had to be carried out.' Denied war crimes: 'The Israeli army is the most moral army in the world.' When asked about civilian casualties, stated: 'War is war.' Blocked UN investigation.

The officers said it was better to demolish buildings than risk soldiers in house-to-house fighting. I still hear the screams.'

heading_label: Passover massacre triggers Operation Defensive Shield
content: Hamas suicide bomber attacks Passover seder at Park Hotel in Netanya, killing 30 Israelis, wounding 140. Deadliest single attack of Second Intifada. heading_label: Operation Defensive Shield begins; other cities attacked first
content: IDF launches Operation Defensive Shield on March 29 with incursion into Ramallah, seizing Arafat's compound. Operations follow in Tulkarm (April 1), Qalqilya (April 1), Bethlehem (April 2). By April 3, six major West Bank cities under Israeli military occupation.

heading_label: Jenin operation begins: 200 tanks surround camp
content: IDF launches major operation in Jenin refugee camp with approximately 200 tanks, Apache helicopters, F-16 jets. Camp home to 14,000 civilians; estimated 80-100 armed Palestinian fighters present. Israel declares area closed military zone. Cuts electricity and water to camp.

heading_label: House-to-house combat begins; medical access blocked
content: IDF begins slow advance through camp using infantry for house-to-house searches. Palestinian fighters engage in fierce resistance using booby traps, explosives, ambushes. IDF blocks ambulances and medical personnel from entering camp. Siege of camp begins—no one allowed in or out for 11 days.

Tank shell and two helicopter-fired TOW anti-tank missiles hit house of Kamal Tawalba (father of 14 children). No fighters present in home. When Tawalba and family try to flee burning house, IDF soldiers fire on them. Example of indiscriminate force documented by Human Rights Watch.

Palestinian fighters lure IDF unit into narrow alley in Hawashin neighborhood. Massive explosives detonated, collapsing buildings on soldiers. 13 Israeli soldiers killed—deadliest single incident for IDF during entire Second Intifada. Israeli military tactics change dramatically after this catastrophic loss.

heading_label: Mass demolitions begin; wheelchair-bound man killed
content: After April 9 ambush, IDF deploys massive D-9 armored bulldozers. Begin systematic demolition of buildings to create wide paths and eliminate ambush sites. Kamal Zghair (57, wheelchair-bound) shot and run over by IDF tanks as he wheels himself home carrying white flag. Mass destruction accelerates.

heading_label: Bulldozers demolish 140+ buildings; many with people inside
content: D-9 bulldozers demolish over 140 buildings in Jenin camp—approximately 10% of entire camp. Eyewitnesses report buildings demolished with families still trapped inside. Some buried alive under rubble. Residents describe hearing people screaming as bulldozers destroyed their homes. IDF prevents rescue attempts.

heading_label: Nurse killed treating wounded; woman dies after 36-hour delay
content: Farwa Jammal (27), uniformed nurse, shot dead by IDF fire while treating injured civilian. Mariam Wishahi (58) injured by shrapnel in her home 'just a few hundred meters from hospital'—IDF repeatedly prevents ambulances from reaching her for 36 hours. She dies without medical treatment.

heading_label: Active combat ends; total siege continues
content: Major fighting ends after 9 days. But IDF maintains absolute siege of camp, preventing anyone from entering—including humanitarian workers, journalists, UN observers. Siege continues for days while Israel attempts to control narrative and prevent documentation of destruction.

heading_label: Medical access finally allowed after 11-day blockade
content: After 11 days (April 4-15), IDF finally allows limited ambulance access to Jenin camp. During blockade, injured combatants and civilians had no access to emergency medical treatment. Sick unable to get care. Direct attacks on medical personnel and denial of medical care constitute serious war crimes.

heading_label: UN Security Council Resolution 1405: fact-finding mission
content: Security Council calls for UN fact-finding mission to investigate Jenin. UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan assembles team. Israel initially agrees then blocks mission through procedural objections. After weeks of obstruction, mission disbanded without ever visiting Jenin. Investigation never occurs.
source: UN SG Report on Blocked Investigation

heading_label: Human Rights Watch investigators access camp
content: Human Rights Watch team of three researchers spends 9 days in Jenin (April 19-28) interviewing over 100 camp residents. Gather detailed victim and witness accounts. Cross-check testimonies. Document extensive destruction. Collect evidence of war crimes. Produce comprehensive 52-page report.

HRW releases comprehensive report: 'During their incursion into the Jenin refugee camp, Israeli forces committed serious violations of international humanitarian law, some amounting prima facie to war crimes.' Report documents 52 Palestinians killed (22 civilians), indiscriminate force, use of human shields, attacks on medical personnel.

heading_label: UN releases limited report; HRW criticizes
content: After Israel blocks fact-finding mission, UN compiles report without first-hand information. Human Rights Watch criticizes: 'watered-down account... doesn't move us forward in terms of establishing the truth.' UN report makes few conclusions about violations or accountability despite serious crimes documented by others.

heading_label: Mass Demolitions with People Inside (War Crime)
content: D-9 bulldozers demolished 140+ buildings, many with families trapped inside. Eyewitnesses reported hearing people screaming as bulldozers destroyed homes. Some residents crushed to death, others buried alive under rubble. Extensive destruction not justified by military necessity constitutes war crime under Geneva Convention Article 147.

14-year-old Muhammad Hawashin shot twice in face and killed while walking with women and children toward hospital (April 3). Kamal Zghair (57, wheelchair-bound) shot and run over by tanks while carrying white flag (April 10). 60-year-old woman killed by helicopter missile in apartment with no armed Palestinians present. HRW documented multiple 'willful or unlawful' civilian killings.

heading_label: Attacks on Medical Personnel and Denial of Medical Care
content: IDF blocked ambulances for 11 days (April 4-15). Repeatedly fired on Red Crescent ambulances. Killed uniformed nurse Farwa Jammal (27) treating wounded. Mariam Wishahi (58) died after 36-hour delay when soldiers prevented ambulance access though she was 'just a few hundred meters from hospital.' Direct attacks on medical personnel and denial of medical care are war crimes.

heading_label: Use of Palestinian Civilians as Human Shields
content: HRW documented IDF using Palestinian civilians as 'human shields'—forcing civilians to enter buildings ahead of soldiers, using civilian homes as military positions while confining inhabitants to rooms, forcing civilians to perform military tasks. Using protected persons to shield military operations violates Geneva Convention Article 28.

heading_label: Indiscriminate and Disproportionate Use of Force

Struck many houses inhabited only by civilians where no fighters present. Tank shells and helicopter missiles hit home of Kamal Tawalba (father of 14) with no fighters present; soldiers then fired on family fleeing burning home. Indiscriminate force violated laws of war.

After UN Security Council Resolution 1405 called for fact-finding mission, Israel initially agreed then systematically blocked investigation through procedural objections. Mission disbanded without visiting Jenin. Obstruction of war crimes investigation suggests consciousness of guilt. Prevented accountability and established culture of impunity.

heading_label: Fourth Geneva Convention Violations - Israeli Forces

heading_label: Misapplication of Legal Framework - Core Violation
content: Law Enforcement vs. Conduct of Hostilities: UN Commission determined Israel unlawfully applies IHL rules on conduct of hostilities to law enforcement in West Bank. Correct framework is international human rights law which strictly limits use of lethal force.

Fourth Geneva Convention Article 27: Protected persons 'shall be treated humanely...protected against all acts of violence.' Killing of 78+ children, journalists, medical obstruction violate this core protection.
Shireen Abu Akleh: Commission found 'on reasonable grounds that Israeli forces used lethal force without justification...and, intentionally or recklessly, violated Abu Akleh's right to life.'
Children: Convention on Rights of Child and Fourth Geneva Convention Article 24 provide special protection. Killing 78+ children, many unarmed, violates these protections.
Duty to Investigate: Geneva Conventions require States investigate grave breaches. Israel has systematically failed to conduct meaningful investigations.

heading_label: Misapplication of Legal Framework - Core Violation
content: Right to Life (ICCPR Article 6): Lethal force only permissible when 'strictly necessary' to protect against imminent threat to life. UN found Israeli forces killed civilians not posing such threats—violations of right to life.

Article 147 (Grave Breaches): 'Wilful killing...wilfully causing great suffering...extensive destruction...not justified by military necessity' are grave breaches. 500+ killings, property destruction meet threshold.
Jenin Operations: Several 2023 operations 'appear to have included unnecessary and disproportionate force.' Use of drones, helicopters in densely populated areas violates proportionality.
Medical Personnel: Geneva Conventions require protection of medical workers. Firing on ambulances, obstructing care, tear-gassing hospital violate absolute protections.
Command Responsibility: Senior military and political officials who knew or should have known of violations and failed to prevent/punish may bear criminal responsibility.

heading_label: Misapplication of Legal Framework - Core Violation

Wounded: Even wounded combatants protected once hors de combat. January 2024 hospital killings of wounded violate Common Article 3.

content: My daughter Yusra, 18, was sitting watching television in our western room. I called out to her but she didn't answer...My son Muhammad came to the door, grabbed me and took me down to the street. I said to him, 'Go find Yusra.' He told me she had been killed...but I wouldn't talk with anyone and said that I wanted Yusra. I wanted to see her and make sure that she was okay, but I could feel that she wasn't all right.

value: Mother/wife, husband and 2 children killed collecting herbs (Jabalya)
content: After lunch on Wednesday, 21 November 2012, my husband Talal asked me to make tea for everyone. Talal went outside to a nearby area that he cultivates to pick some herbs for tea. Two of his children, his son Ayman and daughter 'Abir came along. I began preparing the things for tea when suddenly I heard a powerful explosion from behind the house. I went outside immediately and ran to the place where Talal and the children were. Even before I reached them, I could already see Talal and Ayman lying on the ground, covered in blood...I understood that my husband had apparently been killed instantaneously. Ayman was still moving a little bit. I didn't see my daughter 'Abir. I felt dizzy and weak. Then, apparently, I passed out. [Later told] that 'Abir had also been killed. I screamed and cried hysterically. Three members of my family killed at one blow. I lost them all in an instant, for no reason.

value: Husband of Samaher Qdeih (28), killed in Khuza'ah
content: At around 9:30 PM on 17 November 2012...I decided that we had best go over to the house of my first wife Maha, because it was better protected...I picked up my infant daughter and went over to Maha's house, just seven meters away. Then I returned to get some clothes and a blanket for Mayar. I asked Samaher to bring another blanket and join me. Samaher left the apartment carrying the blanket. Suddenly there was a huge explosion. Chunks of stone went flying all over the place. White smoke filled the courtyard...I found my wife Samaher lying on the ground near the steps of the balcony. I picked her up and saw that her left leg was severed and her clothes torn. Blood was trickling from her mouth. I picked her up and asked that she recite the Shehadatein prayer because I realized that she was badly injured and wouldn't survive. [Samaher died at scene]

value: Grandmother (65), toddler grandson killed in courtyard
content: At about 8:00 o'clock in the morning, three of my grandchildren were playing in front of the house, which is part of the house's compound...Suddenly we heard a huge explosion nearby. We all ran outside to see what happened. I was in shock when I saw that the spot that was hit was right next to the wall that encloses the house, and that it had actually destroyed the wall. I saw my grandson Iyad lying dead on the ground. He had been hit directly by shrapnel. Another of my grandsons, Suhaib, was lying on the ground beside him but he was moving. Sarah was also lying on the ground. I called for an ambulance right away and picked up Iyad. [Iyad, 18 months old, killed; Suhaib (6) and Sarah (4) critically injured]
